reports.title: Cipher Digital Provides Third Quarter 2026 Business Update

desk.headline: Revenue down 63% to $26.7m as bitcoin mining shrinks; first data-centre rent booked; loss per share better than estimate; no financial guidance

other.label: Net income (GAAP)
other.change: lifted by a $127.2m warrant fair-value gain; basic EPS $0.08

results: Revenue fell to $26.7m from $71.7m as the company winds down bitcoin mining and moves to leasing data centres for high-performance computing (HPC).
First HPC rent ($5.9m) came in after rent started at the Black Pearl campus; more data halls at Black Pearl and Barber Lake are due by year-end.
The Barber Lake lease was extended to 20 years with a leading AI lab, lifting contracted revenue there to about $9.1bn (about $5.2bn of new rent).
Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $10.0m; costs rose sharply with staff, admin and interest on new debt (interest expense $59.0m).
Cash was $656m plus $2.2bn restricted; after quarter-end it sold $850m of 0% convertible notes due 2032 and swapped about $165.9m of 2030 notes into shares.

guidance.summary: No revenue or earnings guidance. The company gave only build timelines: Barber Lake data halls to start rent from Q4 2026 to Q1 2027, and Stingray's shell to finish in Q4 2026.

points: Management framed the quarter as the turn to a data-centre landlord, with first HPC rent now flowing.
Pipeline put at about 5.9 GW, helped by a conditional 1 GW base-load classification for the Colchis site in Texas; final classifications are expected in December.
It began building gas pipelines that could feed up to 2.5 GW of on-site power, targeting gas in 2027.
Tenant talks continue for 270 MW of capacity available in 2027 (Reveille and Ulysses sites).
CEO Tyler Page said demand for compute is growing and ties with hyperscalers and AI labs are deepening.
call.source: Prepared business update presentation (Exhibit 99.2) and CEO comments in the press release

watch: Whether Black Pearl and Barber Lake data halls start paying rent on schedule through Q1 2027.
New leases signed on pipeline sites such as Colchis, Reveille and Ulysses.
Interest costs and cash burn as debt has risen to about $6.7bn.
